## Purpose and Entry Points
GeoLibre is a cross-platform, local-first GIS for visualizing, editing, analyzing, and sharing geospatial data. The primary client is a React/TypeScript application bootstrapped by `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/main.tsx` and composed in `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/App.tsx`. It runs as a browser app and as a Tauri native application; the Rust native entry point is `apps/geolibre-desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`.

## Workspace and Domain State
The monorepo separates reusable GIS domain logic from UI/runtime adapters. `packages/core/src/project.ts` defines project-oriented state and serialization, while `packages/core/src/store.ts` and `packages/core/src/types.ts` form the shared state/type boundary. The desktop app consumes these packages rather than owning the core project model, enabling web, native, embed, and Python/Jupyter surfaces to represent the same mapping workspace.

## Map Rendering and Layer Synchronization
`packages/map/src/MapCanvas.tsx` is the primary 2D map surface, with `packages/map/src/CesiumCanvas.tsx` providing globe/3D rendering. `packages/map/src/layer-sync.ts` translates project layers and styles into map-renderer state; `packages/map/src/cesium-layer-sync.ts` performs the equivalent boundary for Cesium. This isolates MapLibre/Cesium-specific lifecycle, style, and rendering concerns from project state and application panels.

## Desktop Shell and Data Ingestion
`apps/geolibre-desktop/src/components/layout/DesktopShell.tsx` organizes the GIS workspace: toolbars, map grid, dialogs, panels, and project actions. `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/components/layout/AddDataDialog.tsx` and its source adapters under `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/components/layout/add-data/sources/` accept local files and remote GIS services (including ArcGIS, OGC, WMS/WFS/WMTS, Postgres, MBTiles, and XYZ). Parsing/load boundaries are implemented in client libraries such as `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/gpkg-reader.ts`, `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/gdal-loader.ts`, and `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/ogc-api-features.ts`.

## Analysis, SQL, and Compute Backends
Processing is registry/runner based: `packages/processing/src/registry.ts` selects tools and `packages/processing/src/runner.ts` executes them through browser WASM, sidecar, or service clients. Spatial SQL and local analytical data paths use DuckDB-WASM (`apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/duckdb-processing.ts`) and PGlite workspace support (`apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/pglite-workspace.ts`). Python-in-browser execution is mediated through Pyodide configuration and console code in `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/pyodide/`.

An optional Python server exposes heavier conversion, raster, vector, SQL, ML, PostGIS, and Whitebox operations through `backend/geolibre_server/geolibre_server/app/main.py` and its route modules. This is a deliberate compute boundary rather than a requirement for core local map use.

## Extensibility and Integrations
The plugin subsystem defines plugin contracts and lifecycle in `packages/plugins/src/plugin-manager.ts` and `packages/plugins/src/types.ts`; the desktop client handles installation, integrity, archive storage, and trust in `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/plugin-registry.ts`, `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/plugin-integrity.ts`, and `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/plugin-trust.ts`. Built-in plugins bridge external APIs and rendering capabilities, including Earth Engine, STAC, Earthdata, routing, deck.gl, raster, temporal, and 3D layers. Native-only boundaries for file I/O, HTTP, and database access are represented by `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/tauri-io.ts` and Rust modules such as `apps/geolibre-desktop/src-tauri/src/native_duckdb.rs`.

## Delivery, Collaboration, and Hosted Services
Tauri v2 packages the same frontend for desktop, Android, and iOS using `apps/geolibre-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` plus platform configurations. Browser deployments can be containerized with `Dockerfile`, `docker/entrypoint.sh`, and `docker/nginx.conf`. Cloud worker services provide distinct external boundaries: AI proxying (`workers/ai-proxy/src/index.ts`), collaborative sessions (`workers/collab/src/index.ts`), tile/reprojection handling (`workers/tiles/src/index.ts`), and shared-project viewing (`workers/viewer/src/index.ts`). Collaboration client/protocol code in `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/collab-client.ts` and `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/collab-protocol.ts` connects the workspace to the collaboration service.

## Jupyter and Python Distribution
The Python package exposes GeoLibre to Jupyter through `python/src/geolibre/geolibre.py`, extension wiring in `python/src/geolibre/_extension.py`, and server integration in `python/src/geolibre/_server.py`. The frontend also embeds notebook/JupyterLite capabilities through `apps/geolibre-desktop/jupyterlite/` and relay code in `apps/geolibre-desktop/src/lib/jupyter-relay.ts`, preserving a bridge between notebook execution and the interactive GIS workspace.
